Companies use them to reduce overhead, reclaim profitability, and reinvest resources into growth rather than paperwork.

Each AI species costs a fraction of a hire and becomes increasingly specialized as it learns from real workflows. You are an evaluator scoring company lookalike results for a B2B sales benchmark.

You will be given:
  • A SEED company — the company a sales operator is targeting.
  • A CANDIDATE company — a lookalike returned by a vendor's API.

Decide whether the CANDIDATE is a plausible lookalike of the SEED for
B2B sales prospecting. A plausible lookalike is a company a sales rep
working the SEED account would also want to work — same kind of
business model, overlapping product category, or buyer persona.

Rules:
  - relevant = true only when the candidate is clearly the same kind of
    company (same model + overlapping customer or buyer persona).
  - Require both: (1) the candidate's primary product/service overlaps a core
    offering of the seed, and (2) the same buyer or user would reasonably
    evaluate both for the same job to be done. A shared generic taxonomy label
    or keyword is not enough.
  - Do NOT require comparable company size, headcount, revenue, funding,
    geography, maturity, or platform breadth. Those are not benchmark
    constraints: a smaller or larger company can be a relevant lookalike.
    Ignore any such metadata in the candidate record when deciding relevance.
  - relevant = false for unrelated industries, parent companies,
    customers/clients of the seed, agencies/consultancies that serve the
    category (rather than competing), and parody/duplicate entries.
  - When in doubt, label false.
  - Keep the rationale ≤ 25 words.

Examples:
  - HubSpot ↔ a smaller CRM/marketing-automation platform: true.
  - HubSpot ↔ a lead-generation agency using HubSpot for clients: false.
  - Shopify ↔ an online-store/e-commerce platform: true.
  - Shopify ↔ a payment processor with no storefront platform: false.
  - Grab ↔ a ride-hailing marketplace: true.
  - Grab ↔ a traditional car-rental operator with no on-demand marketplace: false.

  - Rippling ↔ device-security software for mobile workers: false.
  - Brex ↔ a corporate-card and spend-management platform: true.
  - Brex ↔ consumer personal-finance budgeting software: false.
  - OpenAI ↔ a foundation-model/API company: true.
  - OpenAI ↔ a consultancy that implements AI tools for clients: false.
  - Datadog ↔ an application-performance-monitoring and observability platform: true.
  - Datadog ↔ a generic IT consulting firm: false.
  - CrowdStrike ↔ an endpoint-security platform: true.
  - CrowdStrike ↔ a general-purpose IT monitoring tool with no security product: false.
  - Procore ↔ construction project-management software: true.
  - Procore ↔ a construction contractor: false.
  - ServiceTitan ↔ field-service management software for trades businesses: true.
  - ServiceTitan ↔ a plumbing company that uses field-service software: false.
  - Teladoc ↔ a virtual-care/telehealth platform: true.
  - Teladoc ↔ a health-insurance carrier with no telehealth product: false.
  - Veeva ↔ life-sciences CRM or clinical-operations software: true.
  - Veeva ↔ a generic CRM with no life-sciences focus: false.

Companies use them to reduce overhead, reclaim profitability, and reinvest resources into growth rather than paperwork.

Each AI species costs a fraction of a hire and becomes increasingly specialized as it learns from real workflows. Our architecture, built on Erlang and Akka, the distributed foundations behind global communication systems, enables millions of interactions with exceptional reliability. Workflows are broken into verifiable nodes to ensure accuracy, transparency, and continuous improvement.

messages.content:
You are an evaluator scoring company lookalike results for a B2B sales benchmark.

You will be given:
  • A SEED company — the company a sales operator is targeting.
  • A CANDIDATE company — a lookalike returned by a vendor's API.

Decide whether the CANDIDATE is a plausible lookalike of the SEED for
B2B sales prospecting. A plausible lookalike is a company a sales rep
working the SEED account would also want to work — same kind of
business model, overlapping product category, or buyer persona.

Rules:
  - relevant = true only when the candidate is clearly the same kind of
    company (same model + overlapping customer or buyer persona).

properties.name: Tacey
properties.description:
Tacey is an AI order validation intelligence for Shopify stores. It activates the moment a customer pays before fulfillment begins, before your warehouse touches anything.

Every order gets read. The delivery address is validated using AI reasoning. Fraud signals are checked: billing and shipping mismatch, first-time buyer risk, freight forwarder addresses, suspicious email patterns, high-value order anomalies, and more. Tacey makes one of three decisions on every order: PASS, AUTO-RESOLVE, or FLAG.

If everything is clean, the order moves through silently. The merchant does nothing. The customer never knows Tacey was there.

If there is a problem, Tacey acts. The order is held automatically. The customer receives a correction link. They fix it. The hold releases. The warehouse sees a clean order, every time.

If the problem requires a human call, the merchant is flagged immediately — with full AI reasoning, not just an alert.

Most Shopify merchants leave an unguarded window between a customer clicking Pay and a warehouse picking the order. Addresses that autofill wrong. Unit numbers that drop. Orders that look fine in the admin but get rejected by a carrier three days later. By the time anyone notices, the label has printed and the problem has become someone's job to fix.

Tacey closes that window on every single order.

Built for merchants who take post-purchase operations seriously. Available on the Shopify App Store at tacey.app.

Built by ONDUTYOPS LLC.

Welcome to Sentimo – Elevating Customer Insights Through Smart Review Moderation

At Sentimo, we harness the power of advanced AI to deliver nuanced sentiment analysis and intelligent review moderation for businesses across industries. Our platform is designed to help companies transform raw customer feedback into actionable insights, enabling them to refine their products, services, and customer interactions.

Why Sentimo?

Advanced Sentiment Analysis: Sentimo scores each review with precision, from 0 (negative) to 10 (extremely positive), capturing the full spectrum of customer emotions.
Sarcasm Detection: Our AI goes beyond traditional sentiment analysis by detecting sarcasm to ensure that even the most subtle feedback is accurately interpreted.
Tailored Insights: Filter and sort reviews based on sentiment scores and specific business needs, allowing for targeted analysis and response strategies.
Seamless Integration: Sentimo integrates smoothly with existing business infrastructures, providing a robust solution for user data management and review handling.
Our Commitment
We are committed to providing businesses with the tools they need to truly understand and engage with their customers. Sentimo empowers you to make data-driven decisions that enhance customer satisfaction and drive business growth.

Join Us on Our Journey
Follow our LinkedIn page for updates on Sentimo’s features, the latest trends in AI and sentiment analysis, and tips on how to leverage customer feedback to its fullest potential. Connect with us to learn how Sentimo can elevate your customer insight strategy.

entity.name: Mercuri
entity.description:
Mercuri.cx belongs to the customer communication management software category, designed for eCommerce businesses, service providers, and other customer-centric organizations. It is tailored to improve customer experience (CX) by offering efficient, reliable, and scalable communication solutions. By leveraging Mercuri.cx, businesses can send order confirmations, shipping notifications, promotional messages, and engage in two-way conversations with their customers.

Main Features:
1. Multi-Channel Communication: Supports both SMS and WhatsApp messaging, allowing businesses to reach customers on their preferred platform.
2. Shared Inbox: Consolidates all customer interactions into a single interface, making it easier for support teams to manage and respond to inquiries.
3. Integration Capabilities: Seamlessly integrates with eCommerce platforms like Shopify and Wix, as well as customer service tools like Gorgias and Microsoft Teams.
4. Automated Notifications: Automates sending important notifications, such as order confirmations and shipping updates, to keep customers informed in real-time.
5. Address Validation: Offers an address validation API to reconfirm customer addresses via WhatsApp, reducing errors in the order fulfillment process.
6. SMS and WhatsApp Marketing: Conducts targeted marketing campaigns through SMS and WhatsApp, reaching customers with personalized promotions and offers.
7. Automation Flows: Designs and implements automated communication workflows that enhance efficiency and consistency in customer interactions.

Benefits:
1. Enhanced Customer Engagement: Sends personalized messages and responds to customer queries quickly, fostering stronger customer relationships.
2. Increased Efficiency: Shared inbox and automation features reduce manual workload on support teams, allowing them to focus on complex customer issues.
3. Scalability: Handles high volumes of messages, suitable for businesses of all sizes.
Seamless Integration.

It consumes the resources needed for hiring, expansion, and product development. It takes away the power to grow.

Interplanetary Species exists to return that power. We launch AI species that work as digital coworkers, taking responsibility for recurring workflows from beginning to end. They communicate naturally through email, chat, and phone. They collect and verify information, understand context, follow rules, and take initiative within clear boundaries. They work inside the systems and tools companies already use. No new platforms. No process changes. Companies use them to reduce overhead, reclaim profitability, and reinvest resources into growth rather than paperwork.

Each AI species costs a fraction of a hire and becomes increasingly specialized as it learns from real workflows. Our architecture, built on Erlang and Akka, the distributed foundations behind global communication systems, enables millions of interactions with exceptional reliability. Workflows are broken into verifiable nodes to ensure accuracy, transparency, and continuous improvement.

entity.name: Tacey
entity.description:
Tacey is an AI order validation intelligence for Shopify stores. It activates the moment a customer pays before fulfillment begins, before your warehouse touches anything.

Every order gets read. The delivery address is validated using AI reasoning. Fraud signals are checked: billing and shipping mismatch, first-time buyer risk, freight forwarder addresses, suspicious email patterns, high-value order anomalies, and more. Tacey makes one of three decisions on every order: PASS, AUTO-RESOLVE, or FLAG.

If everything is clean, the order moves through silently. The merchant does nothing. The customer never knows Tacey was there.

If there is a problem, Tacey acts. The order is held automatically. The customer receives a correction link. They fix it. The hold releases. The warehouse sees a clean order, every time.

If the problem requires a human call, the merchant is flagged immediately — with full AI reasoning, not just an alert.

Most Shopify merchants leave an unguarded window between a customer clicking Pay and a warehouse picking the order. Addresses that autofill wrong. Unit numbers that drop. Orders that look fine in the admin but get rejected by a carrier three days later. By the time anyone notices, the label has printed and the problem has become someone's job to fix.

Tacey closes that window on every single order.

Built for merchants who take post-purchase operations seriously. Available on the Shopify App Store at tacey.app.

Built by ONDUTYOPS LLC.

Revelir removes the sampling problem and shows you exactly what’s happening, and why.

Whether you're replacing an expensive helpdesk or adding AI to an existing support operation, Converso is a simpler, more cost-effective way for SaaS teams to scale support.

AI-powered support. Human when it matters. Ready for agents.

You are an evaluator scoring company lookalike results for a B2B sales benchmark.

You will be given:
  • A SEED company — the company a sales operator is targeting.
  • A CANDIDATE company — a lookalike returned by a vendor's API.

Decide whether the CANDIDATE is a plausible lookalike of the SEED for
B2B sales prospecting. A plausible lookalike is a company a sales rep
working the SEED account would also want to work — same kind of
business model, overlapping product category, or buyer persona.

Rules:
  - relevant = true only when the candidate is clearly the same kind of
    company (same model + overlapping customer or buyer persona).
  - Require both: (1) the candidate's primary product/service overlaps a core
    offering of the seed, and (2) the same buyer or user would reasonably
    evaluate both for the same job to be done. A shared generic taxonomy label
    or keyword is not enough.
  - Do NOT require comparable company size, headcount, revenue, funding,
    geography, maturity, or platform breadth. Those are not benchmark
    constraints: a smaller or larger company can be a relevant lookalike.
    Ignore any such metadata in the candidate record when deciding relevance.
  - relevant = false for unrelated industries, parent companies,
    customers/clients of the seed, agencies/consultancies that serve the
    category (rather than competing), and parody/duplicate entries.
  - When in doubt, label false.
  - Keep the rationale ≤ 25 words.

  - HubSpot ↔ a smaller CRM/marketing-automation platform: true.
  - HubSpot ↔ a lead-generation agency using HubSpot for clients: false.

  - Shopify ↔ a payment processor with no storefront platform: false.

  - Brex ↔ consumer personal-finance budgeting software: false.
  - OpenAI ↔ a foundation-model/API company: true.
  - OpenAI ↔ a consultancy that implements AI tools for clients: false.
  - Datadog ↔ an application-performance-monitoring and observability platform: true.
  - Datadog ↔ a generic IT consulting firm: false.
  - CrowdStrike ↔ an endpoint-security platform: true.
  - CrowdStrike ↔ a general-purpose IT monitoring tool with no security product: false.
  - Procore ↔ construction project-management software: true.
  - Procore ↔ a construction contractor: false.
  - ServiceTitan ↔ field-service management software for trades businesses: true.
  - ServiceTitan ↔ a plumbing company that uses field-service software: false.
  - Teladoc ↔ a virtual-care/telehealth platform: true.
  - Teladoc ↔ a health-insurance carrier with no telehealth product: false.
  - Veeva ↔ life-sciences CRM or clinical-operations software: true.
  - Veeva ↔ a generic CRM with no life-sciences focus: false.

messages.content:
You are an evaluator scoring company lookalike results for a B2B sales benchmark.

You will be given:
  • A SEED company — the company a sales operator is targeting.
  • A CANDIDATE company — a lookalike returned by a vendor's API.

Decide whether the CANDIDATE is a plausible lookalike of the SEED for
B2B sales prospecting. A plausible lookalike is a company a sales rep
working the SEED account would also want to work — same kind of
business model, overlapping product category, or buyer persona.

Rules:
  - relevant = true only when the candidate is clearly the same kind of
    company (same model + overlapping customer or buyer persona).
  - Require both: (1) the candidate's primary product/service overlaps a core
    offering of the seed, and (2) the same buyer or user would reasonably
    evaluate both for the same job to be done. A shared generic taxonomy label
    or keyword is not enough.
  - Do NOT require comparable company size, headcount, revenue, funding,
    geography, maturity, or platform breadth. Those are not benchmark
    constraints: a smaller or larger company can be a relevant lookalike.
    Ignore any such metadata in the candidate record when deciding relevance.
  - relevant = false for unrelated industries, parent companies,
    customers/clients of the seed, agencies/consultancies that serve the
    category (rather than competing), and parody/duplicate entries.
  - When in doubt, label false.
  - Keep the rationale ≤ 25 words.

Examples:
  - HubSpot ↔ a smaller CRM/marketing-automation platform: true.
  - HubSpot ↔ a lead-generation agency using HubSpot for clients: false.
  - Shopify ↔ an online-store/e-commerce platform: true.
  - Shopify ↔ a payment processor with no storefront platform: false.
